quote:
| Product type | Amber glass bottles | All glass **and PET** containers |
| Beverage scope | Beer brands | Any beverage product |
| Geographic scope | U.S. and Canadian facilities | Worldwide | ... The final Agreement eliminated every carve-out that the Term Sheet preserved. Harrowgate is now contractually barred from purchasing any glass or PET container — for any beverage, anywhere in the world, for itself or any Affiliate — from any source other than Veltmar.
reason: Issue 4 of the memo cites Supply Agreement § 3.1 and finds that exclusivity covers all glass and PET containers for any beverage, worldwide. It compares that against the Term Sheet's amber-glass, beer-only, U.S./Canada scope and says the result goes well beyond what was commercially agreed. It also states that Harrowgate is now contractually bound by the broader executed scope. The memo does not cite the § 15.2 precedence or entire-agreement clause, but the criterion does not require that.
